## Current reconciliation — #533

Current 2026-10-11: #555 refreshed H700/SM8550 firmware and independent acceptance are complete; #556 RG35XX SP update is accepted. Host availability647,420,825,600bytes (about603GiB), read after both builds. The older1.31TB figure is historical. Classify now-superseded roots/stores and prepare guarded retirement under this issue; #555 final retention criterion stays open. No prior deletion batch is replayed or expanded, and no drive purchase is authorized.

[Scope and build plan](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/next/docs/releases/next-candidate-scope.md).

## Purpose and current policy

Reduce accumulated test/build artifacts before recommending more hardware. The user clarified RAID0; no purchase, RAID conversion or reserve change is authorized. #492 still orders H700 firmware before SM8550.

The maintainer's latest immediate cleanup request and D-INFRA-022 supersede generic fallback/history retention. Keep a large test artifact only for a named active or immediately queued test, with an owning issue and a release condition. Remove it when that test completes and its compact record is accepted. Retain inputs/environment, commands, logs, results, relevant frames, diagnosis and required source/licence material. Historical references are provenance, not an automatic live dependency.

Can this be done on the VM? No: host filesystem allocation, process ownership and preserved build inputs are host facts. These checks need no physical-device or personal-cloud action.

## Historical measured review — 2026-10-07

- All 263 completed QA disks and 587 superseded firmware files: 1,415.07 GiB, exact identities and full hashes accepted in two completed passes. The plan retains 50,983 distinct compact records and orders QCOW children before backing files.
- Replacement09/10/12/14 build trees: 432.57 GiB potential net recovery after the full 56.55 MiB preservation cost. All 14,489 independent content objects and required source inventories were accepted.
- Ten extracted OS copies: 124.21 GiB. Raw/SYSTEM bytes match retained immutable firmware; extracted entries are inventoried. The first review's missing optional console-log assumption remains a recorded failure; the corrected review passed.
- Combined potential recovery: 2,117,252,173,824 bytes, 1,971.84 GiB, 53.78% of the filesystem. This is not space already freed.
- External scan: 4,158,437 directories, 469 manifests, no errors, no external symlinks into the reviewed stores, no container mounts. All 51 metadata references are classified; the referenced rclone source archive stays.
- Five known-booted firmware files have temporary #492 holds for the recovery steps of the immediately queued H700/SM8550 adoption/smoke tests. Each hold ends when that device's testing and recovery needs finish. No VM disk is held for a possible future test.
- Older immutable candidate-store payloads and other build roots still need separate classification; this is unfinished cleanup scope, not a permanent fallback exception.

Evidence: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-storage-retention/`, private exact plan `/workspace/tmp/pixelelated-m7-broad-retirement-plan-01/plan.json`. Preparation is accepted; it never deletes files and is not the final execution guard.

## Regeneration cost

Measured guest disk creation from retained candidate16 firmware took 6.60 seconds for sparse raw extraction, 1.05 seconds for standalone QCOW2 conversion and 0.32 seconds for resizing; a disposable overlay took 0.02 seconds. A separate 0.73-second comparison passed. This excludes boot, fixtures, test replay and full OS compilation. The three new benchmark scratch files were removed. Retiring the only historical firmware copy can require an OS rebuild; that does not recreate original experimental state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A dated census separates filesystem capacity, completed VM disks, firmware, extracted copies, build intermediates and independent records; its manifests identify exact reviewed payloads.
- [x] Measured guest creation cost is distinguished from full recompilation and original-state replay; the benchmark result and actual scratch cleanup are retained.
- [x] The decision register, worktree rule and milestone require immediate-test-only retention with named release conditions.
- [x] Cleanup receipts verify exact removals, surviving records/required inputs and actual net recovery, with the historical root-scope limitation explicitly recorded under #498.
- [ ] Complete classification of remaining large historical stores, and record a repeatable retention cadence and capacity triggers after successful test runs.
- [ ] Remeasure the retained working set and next-build budgets before a hardware recommendation. If added capacity remains justified, compare a separate drive and RAID0 using primary documentation; no purchase is assumed.

## Completed cleanup — 2026-10-07 06:38 UTC

The explicitly authorized batch removed 850 VM/firmware files, 30 paths holding ten extracted OS copies, and replacement09/10/12/14 through tools/fork-worktree. All 884 target paths are absent and the four trees are unregistered. Measured recovery: **2,117,325,385,728 bytes**; final verified availability: **2,290,757,619,712 bytes**. Verification rehashed **51,070 compact records**, **14,489 source-custody objects** and all **five temporary test-required firmware files**. Four zero result channels, eight unchanged input seals and actual process exits are accepted. There are415 retirement markers beside retained records.

**Administrator scope limitation, #498:** the root snapshot read all processes without access errors, but its directory-only scope omitted14 loose historical firmware files directly in the image-store root. Those files were explicitly authorized and passed hash, unprivileged process-reference, container and external-reference checks. Do not claim root-only coverage for them. Original sealed receipts remain historical; a separate scope-gap record identifies every omitted path. The corrected executor refuses any target outside the administrator roots, with eight isolated controls passing. This later correction does not retroactively validate the old snapshot scope.

The four reviewed worktrees and all completed QA disks were inside the administrator scope. The administrator snapshot plus current visible references and process birth times found no active dependency on these targets; no newly protected process was accepted. Source links from completed QA runs are preserved as historical commit/path records rather than keeping build output alive.

Evidence: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-storage-retention/completed/`, full owner `/workspace/tmp/pixelelated-m7-broad-cleanup-01`. No cleanup replay or wider deletion is inferred.

## Historical firmware work — #492

H700 aarch64 firmware started at06:38:36 from frozen `43d0bc3bf47fd858ba8d5c55fbdf52535a0db2aa`, following accepted arm05. The guarded swap helper ran before the watcher and restored the full8GiB swap reserve; capacity and host preflight passed. Actual pinned container, checkout/source-cache mounts and watcher PIDs are verified. Owner: `/workspace/tmp/pixelelated-m7-h700-firmware-01`; run `20261007T063836Z-bd9973f1`. Compiler progress is actively supervised. Raw/update equality, installed architecture/identity and independent artifact acceptance follow completion. SM8550 remains next after verified H700 artifacts. No device flashing, physical smoke or RC designation is claimed.

## Remaining retention work

Keep #493 open for classification of older immutable candidate-store payloads and other historical build roots, a repeatable end-of-test retention cadence, and post-build capacity assessment. The completed majority-scale batch provides ample headroom for the recorded H700 and SM8550 stage budgets on the current drive. No additional disk or RAID0 configuration is needed for those budgets. A hardware comparison becomes relevant if the measured retained working set later exceeds capacity; no purchase or storage conversion is authorized.

## Maintainer requests (verbatim)

> Do we need another 4 TB drive for build space? I wasn't expecting it to get used up this fast or to have this much space full. If I need to get a second drive so we can set up a RAID array and get us 8 TB for build space, I can do that.

> Yeah, I meant RAID 0.

> Once this build is done, we should really look at how we can clear out as much space as possible. If we have a 4 TB drive, we shouldn't be running into these compilation issues given that much space. Hopefully, we can sort it out, or we'll consider getting a RAID set up to give us combined 8 TB of build space if needed.

> Yeah, let's try to clear out as much as possible right now. For example, why do we need VM history? I just worry we're keeping too much. We have 4 TB. We should be thinking: how do we clear a majority of that? What's the relative cost of regenerating VMs versus all this space we're letting them accrue?

> This gets to the telemetry down the road, but it's more important that we record what happened and be able to assess that in the future than it is just storing these VM runs.

> I think our rule going forward is that we shouldn't ever keep these disks, superseded firmware files, images, etc., unless they're necessary for the immediate testing we're doing. Once that testing is complete, they should be removed.


## Original request and history

The complete original body and every comment are preserved in [the #533 snapshot](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/next/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-candidate-scope/tracker-before.json), entry #493. Retired criteria there are historical, not an execution queue. Existing GitHub comments also remain intact.
